# Introduction {.unnumbered}

Welcome to Unit 3! So far, your data has been numbers. Now the data is **categories**: yes or no, bus or car, 9th grade or 10th grade.

When you ask people two questions, a two-way table shows both answers at once. It can show whether the two answers are connected.

***

## What You'll Learn

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

* Read and make two-way tables
* Move between Venn diagrams and two-way tables
* Make relative frequency tables
* Find marginal and conditional distributions
* Decide if two categorical variables are associated

This unit matches **Unit 3: Two-way tables** in Khan Academy's Statistics essentials.

***

## Topics in This Unit

[**Two-Way Tables & Relative Frequency**](3.1_Two-Way_Tables_and_Relative_Frequency.qmd)\
Count answers to two questions at once. Turn counts into percents.

[**Marginal & Conditional Distributions**](3.2_Marginal_and_Conditional_Distributions.qmd)\
Find percents within one group. Decide if two variables are connected.
